newsitem.title: FRANCE: French appliance firm Moulinex swings to profit.
newsitem.headline: French appliance firm Moulinex swings to profit.

text.p: French appliance maker Moulinex, which raised a storm of protest last year when it announced a drastic restructuring plan, said Wednesday that it had returned to profit for the first time since 1991.

Moulinex reported a net profit for the year to March 31 of 29 million francs ($4.96 million), compared with a loss of 702 million ($120 million) in the preceding year that included a 600 million franc ($103 million) provision to pay for the restructuring.

Its operating profit jumped to 160 million francs ($27.4 million) from 54 million francs ($9.2 million), helped by lower raw materials prices, favourable currency shifts and the first benefits of the restructuring.
Chairman Pierre Blayau said the annual results showed the recovery plan was on track, but the fight was not won.
"This is a convalescing company where we are implementing profound changes," he said in an interview.

"There's nothing in the full-year results or assessment of the measures taken that allows us to say success is guaranteed. But the results and achievements of the past year allow us to say we're on track," he said.
The company sparked an outcry a year ago when it announced a plan entailing 2,600 job cuts, a quarter of the staff, and two plant closures in France.
Although the restructuring pales next to a plan announced by Sweden's Electrolux to shut 25 plants and shed 12,000 jobs, Moulinex's staff cuts were proportionately deeper.
After months of tension and negotiations, Moulinex reduced the number of planned staff cuts in France to 1,350 from 2,100 by shortening work schedules at its French factories.
